summary: Jellyfin.Extensions is a grab-bag of static utility extension classes plus a Json/Converters/* subtree of System.Text.Json JsonConverter<T> subclasses. The genuine utility extensions are PORTABLE. The JsonConverter machinery is DEFERRED (in Rust these become serde attributes/helpers in the consuming DTO crate hermit-model, not literal ports). Transliteration/diacritics are portable via the deunicode/any-ascii crates.

portable_types.name: StringExtensions
portable_types.kind: static extension class -> free functions / str methods
portable_types.note: PORTABLE core: Count(char), LeftPart(char), RightPart(char) on char slices; Trimmed(iter<Option<str>>) -> trimmed; TruncateAtNull (cut at first '\0'); GetCleanValue (RemoveDiacritics + lowercase + replace non-letter/digit/space with space + collapse whitespace + trim). RemoveDiacritics/HasDiacritics: port via deunicode or any-ascii + the Diacritics library semantics; also strips non-conforming UTF-16 surrogates + U+FFFD (Rust String is UTF-8 so lone-surrogate case is largely N/A, but keep the U+FFFD strip and the test-vector parity). Transliterated(): wraps ICU4N Transliterator with rule 'Any-Latin; Latin-Ascii; Lower; NFD; [:Nonspacing Mark:] Remove; [:Punctuation:] Remove;' driven by JELLYFIN_TRANSLITERATOR_ID env var -- ICU transliteration has no drop-in Rust equal; approximate with any-ascii/deunicode (lower+punct-strip) or mark this single fn deferred if parity can't be met. NOTE: env-var JELLYFIN_TRANSLITERATOR_ID + regex are magic/config values worth surfacing.

portable_types.name: PathHelper
portable_types.note: PORTABLE. GetSafeLeafFileName: reduce untrusted name to bare leaf, reject empty/'.'/'..'. IsContainedIn(root, candidate): canonicalize both (collapse '..') and check candidate == root or starts with root+separator (guard sibling prefix collision /var/data vs /var/dataset). Use std::path + a normalize that does NOT touch the filesystem (Path.GetFullPath collapses '..' lexically without requiring existence -- do the same, don't use fs::canonicalize which requires the path to exist and would break the temp-path tests).

portable_types.name: DictionaryExtensions
portable_types.note: PORTABLE. GetFirstNotNullNorWhiteSpaceValue(map, key1, key2?, key3?, key4?): return first key whose value is present and not whitespace-only. Model as fn over &HashMap<String,String> + slice/varargs of keys.

portable_types.name: EnumerableExtensions
portable_types.note: PARTIALLY PORTABLE. Contains(iter<str>, value, StringComparison): case-sensitive/insensitive membership -> port as fn taking a comparison mode (Ordinal vs OrdinalIgnoreCase). SingleItemAsEnumerable<T>: trivial (std::iter::once). GetUniqueFlags<T: Enum+Flags>: C#-specific [Flags] enum reflection over Enum.GetValues -- NO idiomatic Rust analog (Rust has no runtime enum-flag reflection); use bitflags crate iter() in the consumer instead -> mark this one method deferred/omit, keep the other two.

portable_types.name: GuidExtensions
portable_types.note: PORTABLE. IsEmpty(guid) = guid == nil/default; IsNullOrEmpty(Option<Guid>) = None or nil. Use the uuid crate (Uuid::is_nil). Untested in this suite but trivial; add smoke tests.

portable_types.name: ShuffleExtensions
portable_types.note: PORTABLE. Fisher-Yates in-place shuffle over a mutable slice; overload with an explicit RNG (for deterministic tests) + a default thread RNG. Use rand crate (SliceRandom::shuffle) or hand-roll the exact loop for parity. Real dep: rand.

portable_types.name: SplitStringExtensions
portable_types.note: PORTABLE. Allocation-free split of a &str on a single char separator yielding subslices. In Rust this is just str::split(sep) returning an iterator of &str -- provide a thin wrapper for API parity (SpanSplit/Split). The C# ref-struct Enumerator is the zero-alloc mechanism Rust gets for free. Untested here.

portable_types.name: ReadOnlyListExtension
portable_types.note: PORTABLE. IndexOf<T:Eq>(slice, value)->isize/Option; FindIndex<T>(slice, predicate)->index; FirstOrDefault<T>(Option<slice>)->Option<&T>. All map to std slice iterator methods (position, iter().position, first). Provide thin fns for parity. Untested here.

portable_types.name: CopyToExtensions
portable_types.note: PORTABLE. CopyTo(source, destination, index=0): copies source[i] into destination[index+i]; MUST panic/error on out-of-range (destination too small or negative/oversized index) to match ArgumentOutOfRangeException test rows. Model over &[T] -> &mut [T] with an offset; bounds-check to reproduce the throwing tests.

portable_types.name: StringBuilderExtensions
portable_types.note: PORTABLE. AppendJoinInSingleQuotes(builder, delimiter, values): append each value wrapped in single quotes joined by a char delimiter (no trailing delimiter). In Rust: write into a &mut String / fmt::Write. Untested here.

portable_types.name: StreamExtensions
portable_types.note: PORTABLE with idiomatic reshaping. ReadAllLines(stream[,encoding]) -> lines of a Read/BufRead (BufRead::lines). ReadAllLinesAsync -> only if async I/O is in scope (tokio) else sync is fine; no test covers it. IsStreamIdenticalAsync(a,b) / IsFileIdenticalAsync(stream,path): byte-for-byte equality of two readers / reader-vs-file. The C# fast paths (MemoryStream TryGetBuffer, ArrayPool, seek-to-0-and-restore, length short-circuit) are impl detail -- reproduce the OBSERVABLE contract: seekable streams compared from start with position restored (file variant) / not restored (stream variant); non-seekable compared from current position; differing lengths -> false; short/partial reads handled. Non-seekable position access throws -> map to a Rust error/Result. StreamComparisonBufferSize=81920 is a magic buffer-size constant worth surfacing as config. Real dep candidate: tokio (only if async kept); std::io suffices for the tested sync-equivalent behavior.

portable_types.name: FileHelper
portable_types.note: PORTABLE. CreateEmpty(path): create-or-truncate an empty file (File::create). Trivial.

portable_types.name: FormattingStreamWriter
portable_types.note: PARTIALLY PORTABLE / reshaped. C# purpose: a StreamWriter that overrides FormatProvider so composite formatting (Write("{0}", 3.14159)) uses InvariantCulture instead of the thread culture (test: de-DE thread culture still yields '3.14159' not '3,14159'). Rust std has no culture-sensitive number formatting -- {} on f64 is already invariant ('.' decimal). So the *behavior under test* is Rust's default. Port as a thin writer wrapper (impl Write) that formats numbers invariantly; the IFormatProvider plumbing itself has no Rust analog. Keep the parity test (invariant decimal output).

deferred.name: JsonBoolNumberConverter
deferred.reason: System.Text.Json JsonConverter<T>: reads bool from a JSON number (0/1) and vice versa. Rust: serde deserialize_with helper on the DTO field, not a standalone type.

deferred.name: JsonBoolStringConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter<T> reading bool from string. -> serde helper in hermit-model.

deferred.name: JsonCommaDelimitedCollectionConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter reading a comma-delimited string into a collection. -> serde deserialize_with helper.

deferred.name: JsonCommaDelimitedCollectionConverterFactory
deferred.reason: JsonConverterFactory picking the generic converter per collection element type. Factory pattern is C# reflection-time machinery; no Rust analog.

deferred.name: JsonDateTimeConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter<DateTime> for custom date parsing. -> serde with chrono/time custom (de)serializer in the DTO.

deferred.name: JsonDefaultStringEnumConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter for string enums with a default/fallback member on unknown values. -> serde enum with #[serde(other)] or custom in hermit-model.

deferred.name: JsonDefaultStringEnumConverterFactory
deferred.reason: JsonConverterFactory for the above; reflection-time, no analog.

deferred.name: JsonDelimitedCollectionConverter
deferred.reason: Abstract base for delimited-collection converters. -> collapses into a serde helper param (delimiter) in Rust.

deferred.name: JsonFlagEnumConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter serializing [Flags] enums as delimited members. -> bitflags + serde in consumer.

deferred.name: JsonFlagEnumConverterFactory
deferred.reason: Factory for the flag-enum converter; reflection-time, no analog.

deferred.name: JsonGuidConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter<Guid> (dashless/formatted). -> serde with uuid crate in hermit-model.

deferred.name: JsonNullableGuidConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter<Guid?>. -> serde Option<Uuid> handling.

deferred.name: JsonNullableStructConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter for Nullable<T> structs. -> Rust Option<T> is native; serde handles it.

deferred.name: JsonNullableStructConverterFactory
deferred.reason: Factory for nullable-struct converter; reflection-time, no analog.

deferred.name: JsonPipeDelimitedCollectionConverter
deferred.reason: Pipe-delimited variant of the delimited-collection converter. -> serde helper (delimiter='|').

deferred.name: JsonPipeDelimitedCollectionConverterFactory
deferred.reason: Factory; reflection-time, no analog.

deferred.name: JsonStringConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter<string> that also reads numbers/bools as strings. -> serde deserialize_with helper on the field.

deferred.name: JsonVersionConverter
deferred.reason: JsonConverter<Version> (System.Version <-> string). -> serde with a Version newtype (e.g. semver or custom) in the consumer.

deferred.name: JsonDefaults
deferred.reason: Static factory building preconfigured JsonSerializerOptions (registers all converters, casing, etc.). Entirely System.Text.Json configuration; in Rust this is per-DTO serde attributes, no central options object.

deferred.name: Utf8JsonExtensions
deferred.reason: Helpers over Utf8JsonReader (System.Text.Json low-level reader). No Rust analog; serde_json handles this internally.

needs_external_crate: deunicode OR any-ascii (transliteration / RemoveDiacritics / Transliterated ASCII-folding)
unicode-normalization (NFD decomposition to match diacritic-stripping semantics precisely)
regex (GetCleanValue punctuation/whitespace collapse; can also be hand-rolled with char classes to avoid the dep)
behavioral_constants: StreamExtensions.StreamComparisonBufferSize = 81920 (I/O compare buffer size) -- surface as config/setting, don't hardcode silently
StringExtensions transliterator env var 'JELLYFIN_TRANSLITERATOR_ID' + default ICU rule string -- config value; rename/surface for hermit
StringExtensions non-conforming-unicode regex (lone surrogates + U+FFFD) -- mostly N/A in UTF-8 Rust; keep the U+FFFD strip for test parity

test_case_breakdown_deferred_json.note: These validate the DEFERRED JsonConverter<T> types. Do NOT port them here; when a hermit-model DTO needs the behavior, reproduce it as a serde helper and re-derive the relevant rows there.

fixture_note: The Json/Models/* files are DTO wrappers used only by the deferred JsonConverter tests; not needed for the portable-type port. No standalone data-file fixtures (all test data is InlineData/MemberData/in-test byte arrays).
